questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, highlighters, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
In the diagram, the curve JK is a country’s production possibility curve. L J good X O K M good Y What could cause the curve to shift to LM?

options.A: a decrease in the participation rate
options.B: a decrease in the unemployment rate
options.C: an increase in the dependency ratio
options.D: an increase in the population of working age

questions.questionText: What is the opportunity cost to a fully employed economy of increasing capital investment?

options.A: a fall in consumption
options.D: a rise in the rate of interest

questions.questionText: Skilled actors deserve to receive a high income because they bring pleasure to people who attend the theatre. What can be concluded about this statement?

options.A: It is a normative statement because both services and goods are economic outputs.
options.B: It is a normative statement because it expresses an opinion.
options.C: It is a positive statement because actors do bring pleasure to people.
options.D: It is a positive statement because greater skill results in higher pay.

questions.questionText: What is the definition of a normal good?

options.A: one where the demand for the good is both price and income elastic
options.B: one where the income elasticity of demand for the good is greater than zero
options.C: one where the proportion of income a consumer spends on the good increases with a rise in income
options.D: one where the quantity demanded increases when the price of the good falls

questions.questionText: A good has a unitary price elasticity of demand and at a price of $20 a firm sells 40 000 units. How many will the firm sell if it charges a price of $5?
The cross elasticity of demand between two products, X and Y, is negative. What would be the immediate effect of a rise in the price of product Y?

options.A: Quantity demanded of product X will fall.
options.B: Supply of product X will rise.
options.C: The cross elasticity of demand will rise.
options.D: The price of product X would rise.

questions.questionText: The table gives the short-run supply schedules of three firms X, Y and Z, which comprise an industry. price quantity supplied (units) ($) firm X firm Y firm Z
The market for tractors is supplied by two firms, X and Y, each initially having 50% of the market.

The diagram shows the equilibrium price (OP) and quantity (OQ) in the market for maize. S P P price P D O Q Q quantity The government wants to achieve a target price of OP . What will be the outcome if the government enters the market and increases the demand by Q-Q ?

options.A: The original equilibrium price will continue to operate.
options.B: The equilibrium price will be at the target price.
options.D: The equilibrium price will be between the target price and the original equilibrium price.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the effect of the imposition of a tax equal to FG on a commodity. S S price u x y v F w G D O quantity Which area represents the reduction in consumer surplus?

options.A: u + v B u + x C u + x + y D x + w

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the average world price of coffee in US cents per pound weight (lb) between 1997 and 2005. The price of coffee, 1997 to 2005 US cents/lb 75 1997 2001 2005 year Which event is consistent with the price behaviour shown in the specified time period?

options.A: a continuous rise in the price of tea between 1997 and 2001
options.B: the entry to the market of new producers of coffee between 1997 and 2001
options.C: a series of good coffee harvests between 2001 and 2005
options.D: increasing health worries about drinking coffee between 2001 and 2005

questions.questionText: What is not a function of the price mechanism?

options.A: to ensure that firms make profits
options.B: to permit consumers to express their preferences
options.D: to signal where resources are required

questions.questionText: In Europe it was decided that farm subsidies would be paid to farmers who protect the environment as well as producing food. What would this mean for farmers who receive the subsidy?

options.A: They must not increase the price of food.
options.B: They must not make excessive profits.
options.C: They must take into account external costs as well as private costs.
options.D: They should produce additional food only if externalities are zero.

questions.questionText: UK supermarkets can buy some vegetables at a lower price from Kenyan farmers than from UK farmers. When the environmental damage caused by transporting the vegetables is taken into account, the social costs of UK supermarkets buying Kenyan vegetables is higher than the social costs of buying UK grown ones. What can be concluded from this information about the buying by UK supermarkets?

options.A: The external benefit of buying vegetables from Kenya is higher than buying them from the UK.
options.B: The external cost of buying vegetables from Kenya is higher than buying them from the UK.
options.C: The private cost of buying vegetables from Kenya is higher than buying them from the UK.
options.D: The social cost of buying vegetables from Kenya is lower than buying them from the UK.

questions.questionText: What can be calculated as part of a government cost-benefit analysis that would not be calculated by a firm seeking only to maximise profits?

options.A: long-run cost

questions.questionText: The government has to choose the best one of four possible sites to locate a port. The benefits and costs of each site are shown in $m in the table. Which site would be chosen? private external private external benefits benefits costs costs
The diagram shows the market for apples. A government maintains a minimum price P by buying apples. D S V W P price Z P
Thailand produces rubber at a lower opportunity cost than China. It does, however, import some rubber from China. What could explain Thailand importing rubber from China?

options.A: China imposes lower tariffs on rubber imports than Thailand.
options.B: China is consuming increasing quantities of rubber in industry.
options.C: Thailand has the absolute but not the comparative advantage in rubber production.
options.D: Thailand wants to avoid the risks involved in overspecialising in rubber production.

questions.questionText: Which argument supports trade protection?

options.A: It might decrease domestic prices.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows that the imposition of a tariff raises price from $10 to $14. domestic supply D price $ domestic demand S 0 20 30 70 100 quantity (millions) What is the value of tax revenue raised?

options.A: $80 million

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the UK trade balance with China and Japan in 2003 and 2004. imports from China imports from Japan £ billion 1000 exports to Japan 600 exports to China 2003 2004 How did the trade balance of the UK change between the start of 2003 and the end of 2004?

options.A: There was a fall in the trade surplus with China.
options.B: There was a fall in the trade surplus with Japan.
options.C: There was a rise in the trade deficit with China.
options.D: There was a rise in the trade deficit with Japan.

questions.questionText: The table gives unemployment rates (%) for four countries in 1993 and 2002. UK Japan France Italy 1993 10.5 2.5 11.4 10.1 2002 5.0 5.4 8.8 8.5 What can be deduced from the table?

options.A: France had the lowest rate of employment in both years.
options.B: Italy had the most employed people in 2002.
options.C: Japan more than doubled its labour productivity between 1993 and 2002.
options.D: The UK created the most jobs between 1993 and 2002.

questions.questionText: In which year did the real value of money rise? Price Index year (base year 2001)

The table shows the price indices and weights for the three commodity groups that make up the calculation of a country’s consumer price index. commodity index weight group X 400 5 Y 120 3 Z 80 2 By how much has the cost of living increased since the base year?

Before 1999 the Brazilian government did not have a desired target rate of inflation. From 1999 it set target rates within an upper and lower boundary. The diagram shows the rate of inflation between 1994 and 2003 and the target rate between 1999 and 2003. Inflation and inflation targets in Brazil, 1994 to 2003 % government target

The UK experienced a growing deficit in its trade in goods during 2003 to 2007 but it also had a stable exchange rate. What could have explained why the trade deficit failed to cause the exchange rate to change?

options.A: Investment income earned by foreigners in the UK was greater than that earned by UK residents on assets held abroad.
options.B: Speculators anticipated that the trade deficit would result in a fall in the value of the pound.
options.C: The UK’s trade in goods deficit was larger than its trade in services surplus.
options.D: The UK attracted a net inflow of foreign direct and portfolio investment.

questions.questionText: Assuming that the supply of exports and imports are perfectly elastic, at which combination of elasticities of demand for imports and exports would a 10% fall in the value of a currency lead to a worsening of the trade account of a country’s balance of payments? elasticity of demand elasticity of demand for exports for imports
The price of a good traded internationally increases. Who would be disadvantaged the most?

options.A: high income countries that pursue a policy of self sufficiency
options.B: high income countries with a balance of payments surplus that export the good
options.C: low income countries dependent on importing the good
options.D: low income countries with alternative suppliers of the good

questions.questionText: A country has a deficit on the current account of its balance of payments. What might help the country to reduce its deficit?

options.A: a decrease in its rate of income tax
options.C: an increase in its level of employment
